current_example.problem:
Find the total area bounded by the polar curve $r=\sin(7\theta),$ shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/d9aa4ff23010048536fbcbadc9cff5dc2fc094895c00814dd9efccdc9750682a.png)
current_example.worked_solution:
First, we want to find the interval for $\theta$ that corresponds to the first petal. Since the curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin, we want to find the values of $\theta$ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
\sin(7\theta) = 0.
$$

This gives us two solutions for $7\theta \in [0,2\pi)\mathbin{:}$

$$
7\theta = 0, \pi \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad \theta=0,\dfrac{\pi}{7}.
$$

As a result, the first petal is traversed for $0 \leq \theta \leq \dfrac{\pi}{7}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/712d56708d2346f502a229c20596e7aa24ce4be13564e9461784c9114c55065a.png)

Since there are $7$ petals, the total area bounded by the polar curve can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{\text{total}} & =7\cdot {A}_{\text{petal}} \\  & =7\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /7}{sin}^{2}⁡(7\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{7}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /7}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(14\theta ))\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\frac{7}{4}(\theta -\frac{1}{14}\operatorname{sin}⁡(14\theta ))|}_{0}^{\pi /7} \\  & =\frac{7}{4}[(\frac{\pi }{7}-\frac{1}{14}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi ))-(0-\frac{1}{14}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))] \\  & =\frac{7}{4}(\frac{\pi }{7}-0) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$
